content.text:
Yes, you need to set a few things up first. The Entire CLI is installed (v0.10.2), but this repo isn't set up for it yet:

- `entire status` says **"not set up"**.
- There's no `.entire/` or `.claude/` folder, and no git hooks are installed.
- **Your Entire login has expired** (`Login for https://eu.auth.entire.io is no longer valid`).
- The GitHub remote (`CL1nu5/munich-ehl-2026-final`) is empty, so your first commit will be the start of the history.

If you commit now, that commit and this Claude session won't be linked to any Entire checkpoint.

**Do this before your first commit:**

1. **Log in again.** It's interactive, so run it yourself:
   ```
   ! entire login
   ```
2. **Turn on Entire for Claude Code in this repo:**
   ```
   entire enable --agent claude-code --checkpoint-backend refs
   ```
   This installs the git hooks, adds Claude Code hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, and creates `.entire/settings.json`. The CLI recommends `refs` for checkpoint storage. If the hackathon organizers told you to use a particular backend or a separate checkpoint repo (`--checkpoint-remote`), use theirs instead.
3. **Restart Claude Code.** Claude Code loads hooks when a session starts, so restarting makes sure the session you build in gets recorded.
4. **Check it worked:** run `entire status`. Then commit `.entire/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.json` together with `readme.md`, so your teammates get the same setup when they clone.

**Also check your commit email.** Your git commits use `linus.pummer@web.de`. If that address isn't linked to your GitHub account, GitHub won't credit the commits to you. It's worth checking if the hackathon looks at who made each commit.

I can run step 2 once you've logged in. Just tell me if you want a different checkpoint backend or your settings kept local only (`--local`).
